classification.difficultyReason: Combine angle sums, straight-line and vertically opposite angles, and properties of parallelograms and rhombuses.

content.prompt: Determine the value of these pronumerals using your angle relationships knowledge.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 8a, first column of upper row
spec.description: Unshaded quadrilateral with two horizontal-looking sides, no parallel marks, a reflex angle at the upper-left vertex and a left extension of the lower side.
spec.mathematics: Interior angles a, b, c and 47 degrees; exterior reflex angle 280 degrees at a; exterior angle 75 degrees adjacent to b.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and unknown letters are visible.

answer.worked:
Angles at a point sum to $360^{\circ}$.
$$\begin{align*}a&=360^{\circ}-280^{\circ}\\&=80^{\circ}\end{align*}$$
Angles on a straight line sum to $180^{\circ}$.
$$\begin{align*}b&=180^{\circ}-75^{\circ}\\&=105^{\circ}\end{align*}$$
The interior angles of a quadrilateral sum to $360^{\circ}$.
$$\begin{align*}c+80^{\circ}+105^{\circ}+47^{\circ}&=360^{\circ}\\c+232^{\circ}&=360^{\circ}\\c&=128^{\circ}\end{align*}$$

spec.sourceRegion: Question 8b, second column of upper row
spec.description: Downward-pointing triangle divided by a horizontal segment into an upper quadrilateral and a lower triangle. No parallel marks.
spec.mathematics: Top angles 72 and 58 degrees; upper-left intersection angle 113 degrees; upper-right intersection d, lower-left intersection e, lower-right intersection f, bottom vertex g.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and unknown letters are visible.

answer.worked:
The interior angles of the upper quadrilateral sum to $360^{\circ}$.
$$\begin{align*}d+72^{\circ}+58^{\circ}+113^{\circ}&=360^{\circ}\\d+243^{\circ}&=360^{\circ}\\d&=117^{\circ}\end{align*}$$
Angles on a straight line sum to $180^{\circ}$.
$$\begin{align*}e&=180^{\circ}-113^{\circ}\\&=67^{\circ}\\f&=180^{\circ}-117^{\circ}\\&=63^{\circ}\end{align*}$$
The angles of the lower triangle sum to $180^{\circ}$.
$$\begin{align*}g+67^{\circ}+63^{\circ}&=180^{\circ}\\g+130^{\circ}&=180^{\circ}\\g&=50^{\circ}\end{align*}$$

spec.sourceRegion: Question 8c, third column of upper row
spec.description: Left triangle and right quadrilateral meet at crossing lines. The quadrilateral retains its upper boundary bend.
spec.mathematics: Left triangle angles 61 degrees, 43 degrees and h. Vertically opposite angle i belongs to the right quadrilateral, whose other angles are 132 degrees, 71 degrees and j.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and unknown letters are visible.

answer.worked:
The angles of the left triangle sum to $180^{\circ}$.
$$\begin{align*}h+61^{\circ}+43^{\circ}&=180^{\circ}\\h+104^{\circ}&=180^{\circ}\\h&=76^{\circ}\end{align*}$$
Vertically opposite angles are equal, so $i=76^{\circ}$.

The interior angles of the right quadrilateral sum to $360^{\circ}$.
$$\begin{align*}j+76^{\circ}+132^{\circ}+71^{\circ}&=360^{\circ}\\j+279^{\circ}&=360^{\circ}\\j&=81^{\circ}\end{align*}$$

spec.sourceRegion: Question 8d, first column of lower row
spec.description: Parallelogram sloping down to the right, with single parallel arrows on horizontal sides and double parallel arrows on sloping sides.
spec.mathematics: Upper-left angle 74 degrees, upper-right angle 106 degrees, lower-right a and lower-left b. Both given angles are retained.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and unknown letters are visible.

answer.worked:
Opposite angles of a parallelogram are equal.
$$\begin{align*}a&=74^{\circ}\\b&=106^{\circ}\end{align*}$$

spec.sourceRegion: Question 8e, second column of lower row
spec.description: Parallelogram sloping up to the right, with distinct single and double parallel arrows, a lower-left reflex angle and a right extension of the lower side.
spec.mathematics: Interior angles c at lower right, d at upper left, e at lower left and f at upper right. Reflex angle 285 degrees at lower left; exterior angle 75 degrees adjacent to c.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and unknown letters are visible.

answer.worked:
Angles at a point sum to $360^{\circ}$.
$$\begin{align*}e&=360^{\circ}-285^{\circ}\\&=75^{\circ}\end{align*}$$
Angles on a straight line sum to $180^{\circ}$.
$$\begin{align*}c&=180^{\circ}-75^{\circ}\\&=105^{\circ}\end{align*}$$
Opposite angles of a parallelogram are equal.
$$\begin{align*}d&=105^{\circ}\\f&=75^{\circ}\end{align*}$$

spec.sourceRegion: Question 8f, third column of lower row
spec.description: Rhombus with one equality tick on each side, an upper-right reflex angle, and lower-right horizontal and sloping extensions.
spec.mathematics: Interior angles i at lower left, j at upper left, h at upper right and g at lower right. Reflex angle 320 degrees at upper right; exterior angle 140 degrees vertically opposite g.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and unknown letters are visible.

answer.worked:
Angles at a point sum to $360^{\circ}$.
$$\begin{align*}h&=360^{\circ}-320^{\circ}\\&=40^{\circ}\end{align*}$$
Vertically opposite angles are equal, so $g=140^{\circ}$.

All four sides are equal, so the quadrilateral is a rhombus. Opposite angles of a rhombus are equal.
$$\begin{align*}i&=h=40^{\circ}\\j&=g=140^{\circ}\end{align*}$$
